review: The hymn is the homeward journey: 1:1–8 is Heb 11:13–16 with Rev 21:23 (the Lamb is its light) and 1 Thess 4:14, and 2:1–8 is 1 Cor 15:55–57 (עֹקֶץ הַמָּוֶת) nearly verbatim with Hos 13:14 and 2 Tim 1:10.
Stanza 1 begins on a split word as the print does (الْـ / ـمَسْكَنِ); the payload keeps the break after אֶל־, so the reader crosses the line into 'the abode' exactly as the Arabic does.

2:5–6 keep the two participles (שׁוֹבֵר וּמְכַתֵּת) for the print's كَاسِرًا سَاحِقًا, using שָׁבַר and כִּתֵּת (Deut 9:21) so the crushing of the tomb door is a physical breaking and not a metaphor of defeat.
2:8 repeats the opening acclamation with the verb changed to sight, following the print's shift from أَمْضِي to عَيْنِي تَرَاه; the Hebrew keeps the same שָׂמֵחַ frame so the two stanzas close alike.
